transcript: Death Becomes Her on Broadway is a textbook musical comedy. It was such a blast seeing a new musical that was hilarious, bold, and visually stunning. It's about two frenemies and a lifelong attempt to one up each other, and along the way they happen upon a chance at eternal, or at least extensive, youth. Chaos ensues and their lives reach a whole new level of ridiculous. Starring Megan Hilty and Jennifer Simard, who are both delightfully hysterical and marvelous together, this show has joke after joke, and pretty much every single one lands. I would describe a lot of the jokes as vulgar and cynical but not overly dark. And the comedy remains in full swing during the music too, along with the slapstick moments and the flamboyant staging. The costuming is stellar and the sets and lighting design are so fun. It really seems like no expense was spared when mounting this, and the vibes are simply immaculate so it was worth it. This is based on a movie which I've never seen so clearly you don't need to have seen that to love this. And I'll be the first to say I'm not always the most welcoming towards screen to stage adaptations, but I really hope the critics don't pan this one just to be pretentious, like this is good theater. It knows exactly what it is, it sticks to it and it succeeds at it. Two thumbs up for me. With that, another playbill for my collection.
